edge: With same-named cells in multiple libraries, use a library-qualified cell clause and verify that only the named library and cell are selected.
positive: Use an unqualified cell clause and verify that every instance of the named cell is selected.

edge: Use an unqualified cell identifier to exercise omission of the optional library qualifier.
negative: Write a cell clause without its required cell identifier.
positive: Use both library-qualified and unqualified cell clauses.

edge: Specify one library name and contrast omission of the mechanism.
negative: Attempt to provide a path or new library definition where only library names are accepted.
notes: The option spelling is tool-specific; -L is only recommended.
positive: Specify two mapped library names in reverse map order and verify command-line binding order.

edge: Exercise a primitive or program instance separately from a module instance.
positive: Apply configuration binding rules to module, primitive, interface, and program instances.

edge: Supply a same-named unrelated cell in another library.
positive: Supply several uninstantiated modules and a config design statement selecting one top.

edge: Use names of different design-element kinds near a config name to exercise namespace handling.
notes: Requires a library/configuration flow that can observe selected source descriptions.
positive: Declare a named config and select it to govern source binding for a design.

edge: Use a localparam initialized by a literal at an index boundary.
negative: Use a design parameter or other identifier as the index.
positive: Index an instance array using a literal or configuration localparam.

edge: Place the configured instance adjacent to, but not within, a generate scope.
negative: Use an override hierarchical reference through a generate block scope.
positive: Use an override reference through ordinary instance scopes.

edge: Contrast a scalar instance with one element of an instance array.
negative: Use an override hierarchical reference through an array-of-instances scope.
positive: Use an override reference through a scalar instance hierarchy.

edge: Omit one library and retain fallback libraries for absent cells.
positive: Reverse map order in a config liblist and verify config-directed binding.

edge: Declare multiple configuration localparams and omit the initializer from only one.
negative: Declare a configuration localparam without assigning a value.
positive: Declare a configuration localparam with a literal initializer.

edge: Use sized and unsized literal forms.
negative: Initialize a configuration localparam from an identifier or nonliteral expression.
positive: Initialize configuration localparams with integer and string literals.

edge: Use a uniquely named configuration to distinguish the collision condition.
negative: Try to denote a same-named configuration without :config.
positive: Reference a same-named configuration with :config.

edge: Target parameters at different levels to distinguish the precedence condition.
positive: Apply config and defparam overrides to one parameter at the same level and observe the config value.

edge: Use a literal expression requiring no function.
negative: Call a user-defined constant function in an override.
positive: Use a built-in constant system function in an override.

edge: Use same-named packages in distinct libraries while configuring nearby module instances.
negative: Attempt to use a configuration to change which package is bound.
positive: Use a package normally while configuration rules alter only module-instance binding.

edge: Shadow a name in parent and outer scopes to observe parent-first resolution.
negative: Rely on a same-named identifier visible only in another scope.
positive: Reference a parameter visible in the configured instance's parent scope.

edge: Use no rules after design and include an optional identifier after endconfig.
negative: Use a configuration-rule combination absent from the grammar.
positive: Parse each configuration-rule alternative and optional grammar form.

edge: Contrast a design-level parameter override with an instance-specific override.
positive: Override a parameter for a selected instance through a configuration.

edge: Use instance and cell selection clauses with use expansions while retaining a legal default liblist.
negative: Pair a default selection clause with a use expansion clause.
positive: Use a default selection clause with a liblist expansion.

edge: Use distinct nondefault instance or cell rules alongside one default expansion.
negative: Specify two default clauses for the same permitted expansion clause.
positive: Specify one default liblist expansion clause.

edge: Bind descendants at multiple hierarchy depths through the same default rule.
negative: Provide no matching cell in any library of the applicable default liblist.
positive: Bind several descendants through a default liblist containing their source library.

edge: Place a same-named child cell in another library to verify parent-library fallback.
positive: Bind a child from its parent's library with no selected liblist and with an empty selected liblist.

edge: Apply default at multiple hierarchy depths.
positive: Let unmatched siblings use a default rule while one sibling has an instance rule.

edge: Use no config rules after design.
negative: Place a config rule before design.
positive: Place design before default, instance, and cell rules.

edge: Disambiguate same-named module and configuration cells.
negative: Name a configuration itself as a design cell.
positive: Name a top module in a design statement when a same-named configuration also exists.

edge: Specify multiple configured top-level design elements.
negative: Select a library-qualified top cell absent from that library.
positive: Select a top module with a library-qualified name and provide that cell in the named library.

edge: Mix library-qualified and unqualified top cells in the same design statement.
positive: List two top-level module cells in one design statement and elaborate both hierarchies.

edge: Compile the versions in separate invocations.
positive: Compile two successive versions of one cell and observe the latter definition binding.

edge: Reset a parameter whose instantiation supplied a nondefault value.
positive: Override one parameter with .P() and observe its module default while other parameter values remain unchanged.

edge: Contrast use #() with a single empty named override .P().
positive: Apply use #() to an instance with several nondefault instantiation values and observe all module defaults.

edge: Use multiple top-level modules whose descendant hierarchies all require binding.
negative: Instantiate a child for which no source module definition can be located.
notes: Observe elaboration success or failure rather than diagnostic wording.
positive: Build a complete hierarchy in which every instantiated module resolves to a source definition.

edge: Exercise both zero-directory and multiple-directory matches.
positive: Use ... to match a file below multiple directory levels.

edge: Place the map file outside the process working directory to distinguish the base.
positive: Reference a mapped source through ./ relative to the map file.

edge: Combine .. with a following directory and filename wildcard.
positive: Reference a mapped source through .. from a nested map-file directory.

edge: Contrast zero-, one-, and two-character candidate substrings.
positive: Match one-character file-name components with ?.

edge: Exercise both zero-character and multi-character matches without crossing a directory boundary.
positive: Match file-name prefixes and suffixes with *.

edge: Nest configurations through more than one subtree level.
positive: Bind one subtree to a nested config with distinct descendant rules relative to its own top.

edge: Contrast a simple identifier expression with a hierarchical identifier expression.
negative: Add a literal to a hierarchical identifier.
positive: Set an override directly to one hierarchical identifier.

edge: Nest included map files.
negative: Use a malformed include statement or nonexistent included path.
positive: Include a map whose declarations are needed after the include point.

edge: Target the top-level instance path and a deeply nested path.
negative: Use an instance path rooted outside the design statement's tops.
positive: Target a nested instance with a hierarchy rooted at a configured top.

edge: Override a deeply nested instance while ancestors use default binding.
notes: Observe which implementation is elaborated, not source-file names themselves.
positive: Give one instance a gate-library rule while its sibling remains governed by the RTL default liblist.

edge: Override an inherited liblist at a descendant and distinguish the two subtrees.
positive: Select a liblist for one instance and verify that its descendants inherit it.

edge: Make the first library lack the cell and verify fallback to the next listed library.
positive: Place same-named cells in two listed libraries and verify binding to the first.

edge: Place output in two instances bound to different library cells.
positive: Execute $display with %l and %L inside a library-bound module and compare its library.cell identity.

edge: Map distinct kinds of design elements having valid cell names.
negative: Attempt to map a design element into a differently named cell.
positive: Map a module into a library cell with the module's name.

edge: Use empty map text, an empty semicolon description, and multiple source or include-directory paths.
negative: Omit a required semicolon from a library or include statement.
notes: Use the formal production as the authority for exact alternatives.
positive: Parse every library-description alternative from the formal grammar.

edge: Specify an empty map.
positive: Specify one and multiple map files.

edge: Parse multiple source files after one map.
positive: Parse source after reading its applicable map.

edge: Use the same relative spelling in map files located in different directories.
positive: Resolve relative paths independently in a root map and a nested included map.

edge: Overlap patterns within one library versus across two libraries.
negative: Make the same file remain matched by two libraries after specificity resolution.
notes: Do not depend on diagnostic wording.
positive: Use nonoverlapping library path specifications.

edge: Reverse their order.
positive: Use two maps with observably order-dependent declarations.

edge: Override one of several parameters by name.
negative: Attempt a positional configuration parameter override.
positive: Override parameters by name from a configuration.

edge: Use different cell names whose first containing libraries differ.
positive: Declare same-named cells in two libraries and omit a config; verify the earlier map declaration wins.

edge: Target the nested-config boundary instance versus a child below it.
negative: From an outer configuration, target a descendant below an instance bound to another config.
positive: Place descendant rules within the nested configuration itself.

edge: Place several top cells within the sole design statement.
negative: Provide zero or two design statements.
positive: Provide one design statement in a configuration.

edge: Exercise a hierarchical parent identifier at the legal boundary.
negative: Use a parent-binding identifier form prohibited in bind.
positive: Use a parent-scope identifier form also legal for bind.

edge: Place other-suffix files beside .v files to verify the matching set.
positive: Use ./*.v and *.v against identical map-file-directory fixtures and compare mapped files.

edge: Exercise each adjacent priority pair separately.
positive: Overlap explicit-name, wildcard-name, and directory-ending specifications and verify the most specific wins.

edge: Compare the trailing / form with the corresponding /* form.
positive: Use a trailing-directory path to map every file directly in that directory.

edge: Precompile cells over multiple compilation invocations.
notes: Invocation syntax and compiled-object format are tool-specific.
positive: Precompile configured design cells, then reference the compiled design objects on a later command line.

edge: Use a qualified cell selector with a use clause instead.
negative: Combine a library-qualified cell selector with liblist.
positive: Use an unqualified cell with liblist.

edge: Compile replacement definitions in separate invocations to distinguish the stated single-invocation condition.
notes: Check required warning presence, not wording; do not infer that other situations forbid warnings.
positive: Compile two same-named modules into one library in one invocation and observe a warning.

edge: Bind multiple tops sharing compiled descendants.
positive: Give the binder only top-cell selection and persisted compiled descendants.

edge: Recompile one cell before binding while retaining the others.
negative: Leave one required descendant cell uncompiled when binding starts.
positive: Precompile all hierarchy cells over multiple invocations before binding.

edge: Reference the precompiled config by its library and cell name.
negative: Attempt separate-compilation binding with an uncompiled config.
positive: Precompile both selected cells and the governing config before binding.

edge: Use a tool-selected non-source filesystem representation.
negative: Discard required compiled cells before the binding invocation.
positive: Compile a library in one invocation and bind its persisted cells in a later invocation.

edge: Use an up-to-date previously compiled cell, which an implementation may optionally skip recompiling.
notes: Do not require recompilation when the source is unchanged; the source explicitly permits that optimization.
positive: Supply one used and one unused cell description and verify that both are mapped into their libraries.

edge: Place a same-named cell only in a persisted library but omit its source from the single-pass command line.
negative: Require binding to a cell absent from the invocation's source set.
positive: Supply every needed source description on the command line and bind only among that set.

edge: Place multiple cell definitions in one matched source file.
positive: Map source files with distinct path specifications and bind cells from their matching libraries.

edge: Contrast one mapped and one unmapped source file.
positive: Compile an unmapped source and bind its design element from work.

edge: Contrast qualified and unqualified top cells.
negative: Provide the unqualified top only in another library.
positive: Place config and unqualified top cell in one library.

edge: Use qualified and unqualified exact cell names while controlling inherited-library behavior separately.
positive: Use instance-use and cell-use rules to select exact implementations.

edge: Use default with liblist while separate instance and cell rules use exact bindings.
negative: Pair a use clause with a default selection clause.
positive: Pair use clauses with instance and cell selection clauses.

edge: Place a same-named cell in another library to verify parent-library inheritance.
positive: Use an unqualified cell name that exists in the parent cell's library.

edge: Provide separate rules selecting a binding and a library list for the same scope.
positive: Apply a use binding at one instance and verify descendants or siblings retain the independently selected liblist.

edge: Bind a module instance to a cell whose name differs from its module name.
positive: Query vpiCell on instances bound to differently named cells.

edge: Query parent and nested-config descendants controlled by different configs.
positive: Query vpiConfig for instances controlled by a named config.

edge: Query modules at multiple hierarchy depths.
positive: Query vpiLibrary for modules compiled into two named libraries.
